subject: Request: carveout & shared-responsibility for private deployment SLA (Zenorix)
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@zenorix.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Request for carveout and shared-responsibility language for private deployment

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to move forward with Redwood Private inside our colo footprint, but we need to lock down SLA language that reflects the reality: Zenorix will manage the customer-controlled Kubernetes cluster, VPC routing, and some of the egress peering/SD-WAN. That infrastructure contributes tail latency and occasional packet loss outside of Redwood's runtime.

Heads-up on two specific asks from our side:
- Carve out: Zenorix requests that any availability/latency SLOs exclude customer-controlled network tail events and customer-managed control plane maintenance windows.
- Shared responsibility: we propose an appendix that enumerates owner-of-truth for networking, DNS, KMS, and node maintenance. When incidents originate in our infra, Redwood would not be liable for SLA credits.

I've attached network traces from last week's test (zenorix_network_traces_20280314.zip) and a quick draft of the appendix (zenorix-sla-appendix-draft-v1.docx). We can provide a Grafana read-only link and weekly packet-capture summaries if that helps with evidence.

Target timeline: legal wants a restated SLA and appendix by end of month (Mar 31). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 99.5% availability guarantee for the Redwood-managed runtime inside the private deployment, with the network-tail carveout as described? If so, we'll hand this to legal and engineering to finalize.

Thanks —
Priya Rao
Head of Platform Ops
Zenorix Therapeutics
priya.rao@zenorix.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@zenorix.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for carveout and shared-responsibility language for private deployment

Priya —

Appreciate the detailed note and the artifacts. Quick read: the ask is reasonable in principle, but we do need concrete definitions and evidence gates so we can operate cleanly when incidents occur. Two immediate asks from our side:

1) Definition: Can we align on a short definition for "customer network tail event" (e.g., any packet loss/latency > X ms on hops outside of the Redwood Private data path, or events attributable to customer peer/router ASNs)?

2) Evidence & process: For any uptime/latency dispute we'll need either (a) the Grafana traces and pcap you attached, or (b) a jointly-agreed forensic checklist (timestamps, flow ids, SRv6/MPLS path evidence) within 10 business days of the incident.

Operationally, Redwood is willing to: guarantee the model-serving runtime (inference engine + KV cache + local scheduling) at 99.95% uptime for the service processes we host in the private deployment. However, we will accept an appendix that explicitly excludes customer-managed network components from credit calculations. For latency SLOs we can commit to median and 95th percentile token latency for in-cluster processing; we will not take responsibility for customer egress latency beyond the private node's uplink.

Next steps from my side: Monica (Sales) — can you confirm whether the customer is willing to accept credits-only for certain categories of failures, and whether legal expects any monetary cap? Marcus (Infra) — please review the technical evidence checklist and tell me what minimum fields we require for an attribution decision.

If we can get agreement on these points, I'll circulate a Redwood-first draft appendix for Zenorix legal to redline.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

--
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

Thanks — yes, we can do both. Proposed clarifications from our side:
- "Customer network tail event" = any observed RTT > 250ms on hops outside the private node uplink, or > 1% packet loss on the end-to-end flow where the last-mile ASN is Zenorix-controlled. We can provide the ASN lists and peering IP blocks for the nodes.
- Evidence: we'll give Grafana read-only access (https://zenorix-grafana.example.com/d/abcdef/llm-serving?orgId=1) and will retain pcap snapshots for 14 days; we can push longer retention into a storage bucket behind a signed URL for up to 90 days on request.

On credits and legal: legal has asked that Redwood accept a credits-only remedy for customer-network-caused downtime, and that any monetary exposure be capped at 12 months of subscription revenue for the contract tier. Is that acceptable? If not, please identify what cap you would require.

Finally — we can do a brief joint runbook review next week (Mar 21) to align on forensic checklist fields. Please include Marcus and Monica on the invite.

Regards,
Priya

Priya Rao
Head of Platform Ops
Zenorix Therapeutics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Summary of proposed carveout language & next steps (Zenorix)

Folks —

Summary from the thread and the artifacts Priya sent:

1) Definitions we need to lock:
   - "Customer network tail event": RTT > 250ms on hops external to Redwood-managed private node uplink, or sustained packet loss > 1% on flows where the last-hop ASN is within the customer-provided list.
   - "Redwood-managed runtime": model-serving processes, KV cache, scheduler, and local health agents running on the private node(s).

2) Evidence & retention:
   - Zenorix provides Grafana read-only link and pcap snapshots (14 days) + signed URL for up to 90 days on request.
   - For attribution, require (a) timestamped flow IDs, (b) packet captures with hop RTTs, (c) private node system logs from Redwood (we already retain 90 days).

3) Remedy & caps:
   - Redwood will provide credits-only for events attributable to the customer network tail.
   - Customer asked for monetary cap = 12 months ARR. Redwood legal to propose counter (suggest number, e.g., 6 months) — flagging this for legal negotiation.

4) Operational:
   - Joint runbook review scheduled: Wed, Mar 21 09:00 PT (invite to be sent).
   - Action: Rishi to produce a Redwood-first appendix draft and circulate to Zenorix legal; Monica to confirm commercial acceptability of credits-only posture; Marcus to provide the minimal forensic checklist fields by EOD Mon, Mar 20.

I'll draft the appendix language that incorporates the definitions above and the evidence checklist. If you want, I can also include a short sample incident decision flow (who signs off on attribution within 10 business days).

Marcus

Redwood Inference
